documents.title: Obstetrics: Prenatal Course Summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Prenatal summary for primary care, visits 11/24/2025 through 01/05/2026.

G1P0, EDD 03/02/2026.
11/24/2025 (26w0d): 1-hour 50 g glucose challenge 112 mg/dL, normal. Fundal height and fetal heart tones appropriate.
12/08/2025 (28w0d): Tdap given. Feels well, good fetal movement.
01/05/2026 (32w0d): RSV vaccine (Abrysvo) given. Fundal height measuring with dates; BP normal; no edema. Pregnancy progressing normally.
Medications: prenatal vitamin. Allergies: NKDA.
Next visits every 2 weeks, then weekly from 36 weeks.
Obstetrics

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT RECORD. Regional hospital ED, seen 02/04/2026. Received by the practice 02/09/2026.

CC: fever and aches, 36 weeks pregnant.

HPI: 28F G1P0 at 36w2d (EDD 03/02/2026) with two days of fever, feeling run down and diffuse muscle aches. Also some mild crampy lower abdominal discomfort and a little more vaginal discharge than usual. Denies fluid leaking or contractions. No travel, no one sick at home. Pregnancy uncomplicated to date per patient and OB records. On questioning, she ate deli meats from the fridge and imported soft cheeses at a family picnic five days ago. History of tinea corporis of the forearm this pregnancy, treated by dermatology, resolved.
Meds: prenatal vitamin. Allergies: NKDA.
PSH: tonsillectomy. Social: never smoker, no alcohol.

Exam: T 38.6 C (101.5 F); other vitals per nursing flowsheet. Fatigued appearing, alert and oriented. Neck supple, no meningismus. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen gravid, soft, uterus nontender. No CVA tenderness. Fetal heart tones present, reassuring on monitoring.

Labs: WBC 14.6, mild leukocytosis. BMP and lactate within normal limits. UA negative. Urine and blood cultures (2 sets) sent.

MDM: febrile illness in late pregnancy after high-risk foods; concern for listeriosis. Started ampicillin 2 g IV every 4 hours after cultures. Discussed with OB on call; admitted to the obstetric service for IV antibiotics and fetal monitoring.
Disposition: admitted, stable.

events.reason: Febrile illness in pregnancy, suspected listeriosis

documents.title: Discharge Summary, Obstetric Service
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY. Admitted 02/04/2026 from the ED, discharged 02/08/2026. Received 02/09/2026.

Diagnosis: listeriosis (Listeria monocytogenes bacteremia) in pregnancy, 36 weeks.

Course: 28-year-old G1P0 admitted at 36w2d with fever after eating deli meat and soft cheese. Started on ampicillin 2 g IV every 4 hours in the ED after cultures. Both admission blood culture sets grew Listeria monocytogenes, ampicillin-susceptible, reported 02/06. She was afebrile from hospital day 2 and the myalgias and cramping settled. Repeat blood cultures 02/06 negative (final no growth). Continuous and then twice-daily fetal monitoring reassuring; nonstress tests reactive throughout. No contractions, membranes intact, no labor.

A PICC line was placed in the right arm on 02/07 for home infusion.

Discharge medications: ampicillin 2 g IV every 4 hours via home infusion, last dose 02/17/2026 to complete 14 days; prenatal vitamin daily.
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: home infusion nursing for PICC care and removal; OB clinic twice weekly for nonstress tests until delivery; primary care this week. Return for fever, contractions, leaking fluid or decreased fetal movement. Avoid deli meats, unpasteurized cheeses and refrigerated smoked fish for the rest of the pregnancy.
Obstetrics

documents.title: Home Infusion Nursing Visit
documents.author: home infusion RN
documents.body:
Home infusion nursing visit 02/18/2026. Received 02/19/2026.
IV ampicillin course completed with the final dose 02/17/2026, 14 days total. No missed doses. Afebrile. Right arm PICC removed intact today, tip intact, pressure held, site clean and dry with dressing applied. No arm swelling. Patient instructed on site care. Discharged from home infusion services.

documents.title: Delivery Discharge Summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OBSTETRIC DISCHARGE SUMMARY. Admitted 02/23/2026 in labor, discharged 02/25/2026. Received 02/27/2026.

29-year-old G1P0 at 39w0d, admitted in spontaneous labor. Antepartum course notable for Listeria bacteremia at 36 weeks treated with 14 days of IV ampicillin (completed 02/17), blood cultures cleared. Afebrile throughout labor.

Uncomplicated spontaneous vaginal delivery 02/23/2026 of a liveborn girl, 3240 g, Apgars 8 and 9. Placenta delivered intact. Pediatrics examined the newborn given the maternal infection: well appearing, no signs of infection, routine newborn care.

Postpartum course routine; mother afebrile and well. Now G1P1.
Discharge medications: prenatal vitamin daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: OB postpartum visit in 6 weeks; pediatrics for the baby.
Obstetrics

documents.title: Obstetrics: Postpartum Visit
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Postpartum visit 04/06/2026, 6 weeks after an uncomplicated vaginal delivery. Copy to primary care.
Feeling well. Bleeding stopped. No fevers. Sleeping when the baby sleeps; good support at home. Postpartum mood screen normal.
Exam: BP normal. Breasts normal. Abdomen soft, uterus involuted. Perineum healed. 
Assessment: normal postpartum recovery. Continue prenatal vitamin. Routine gynecologic care; next Pap per screening guidelines. Return to primary care for general care.
Obstetrics
